title: Other albums in the works: Art Hodes group and Doc Cheatham
summary: A small-group Art Hodes album, a Doc Cheatham date, and a Buck session including 'Brother, Can You Spare a Dime'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: and I have another album that I made at the same time I was down there, but it's made with a smaller group, just a piano, bass and drums with a young man on clarinet, I don't know his name offhand.
But this is with Art Hodes--
This one is with Art Hodes group here, it's a good traditional-type jazz band.
The record we're talking about now is out on the Audiophile record label and was AP 128. The small group record you're talking about has not yet been issued.
No. Right.
Hopefully it will be soon.
Uh-huh.
And then you were telling me you also did some material with Doc Cheatham.

Oh, yeah, well, that's going to be released, too. We made that this year. Joe Robertson had called me in, he had arranged for a series of jazz concerts down there in Raleigh and Whispering Pines and the area down there and of course

George Buck contacted Joe and he was interested in making another album because we were down there on the tour or the festival, whatever you want to call it, with Herb Hall and Doc Cheatham and Red Richards and [Joe] Buck was anxious to get them on the records so we went to Charlotte, South Carolina, and made the album in which he dug up some more songs that I hadn't -- quite a few of them are Duke Ellington's tunes which I had never done before --
Oh, how terrific.

And we managed to do -- I didn't know about you, a tune that I had been carrying around with me for quite a long time, but never had a chance to do. In fact it was on a session that we had made but it was rejected or never released.
That's right, wasn't that back in 1955, 1956?
That's right.
Which is what we started about today.
And also in this album you're going to hear 'Brother, Can You Spare a Dime.'
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Well, if you're speaking on behalf of the House that Jack Built --
"Brother, Can You Spare a Dime."
You never know, you may be favored.

Well, I spoke to Wendell Echols who was a production coordinator. He didn't get to the last session that we made, but he's heard the tape and they're quite pleased with it. I was kind of tired when we made it, but I'm happy to note it turned out all right and of course I did hear the tape of the album that I made at the same time we made "We Just Couldn't Say Goodbye." And that's a very good album, too.
Oh, very good.

And it has some tunes in there that I've not done before and also it would be worth including in my repertoire like "Can't We Talk It Over" and things like that. I heard the album when I was down there -- I heard the tape and it sounded very good. So I guess it will be out, maybe next year.
